title: Signature requests are visible through their host row
detail: `createSignatureFeature` takes the required `hostEntities`, and every `signature:write:request` payload carries `hostType` and `hostId`. A user sees, signs, issues links for, revokes and cancels a request only while the host row is readable to them through the host entity's own `access.read`; otherwise the answer is 404 like a missing record. The request list filters in SQL, so `total`, `offset` and `aggregate` work again and the cursor is a plain cursor. The signer list requires exactly one `requestId` filter for every user (403 otherwise) and answers an empty page for a request whose host the user cannot read. `authorizeSubject`, `unscopedRoles`, `AuthorizeSignatureSubject` and `SignatureSubject` are removed. `subjectType` and `subjectId` stay as a free label.
migration: Pass `hostEntities` (registered entity names without their own `parentRef`) and add `hostType`/`hostId` to every request payload; move the visibility rule from `authorizeSubject` into `access.read` of the host entity. Run `kumiko-schema generate` and ship the migration for the columns `host_type` and `host_id` and the index on `read_signature_requests`. Requests stored without a host stay invisible.

title: forget-signer checks the host record
detail: signature:write:forget-signer loads the signer's request and its host record with the caller's rights, like revoke-link. A caller who cannot read the host (for example a data protection officer without read access to the lease) gets 404 and the signer stays.
migration: Code that calls createForgetSignerHandler directly passes the signature request executor. Erasing signers of records outside the caller's read rights runs through a role that can read the host or through forget-subject.

title: authorizeSubject receives the subject scope context instead of the full handler context
migration: The ctx argument of `authorizeSubject` (`AuthorizeSignatureSubject`, `AuthorizeDocumentDraftSubject`) is now `SubjectScopeContext` from the shared barrel: `db`, `registry` and `services` only, because the check also runs in `beforeTransaction`, before a draft is printed. A callback that reads only these compiles unchanged; one that used `ctx.user`, `ctx.dispatch` or `ctx.events` takes the user from its second argument and reads through `ctx.db` instead.

title: Empty signature images are rejected on any background
List cursor of subject-scoped users is sealed
Unrecoverable finalisation ends in status failed
Empty signatures are rejected on every background
Subject check for the signature feature and a readable-file check on requests
detail: `createSignatureFeature({ ..., authorizeSubject, unscopedRoles })`: `authorizeSubject(ctx, user, { subjectType, subjectId })` runs for `request`, `cancel`, `issue-link`, `revoke-link`, `sign-in-person` and the queries, except for users holding a role of `unscopedRoles`; `false` answers like a missing record (not found, `null` or an empty page). `signatureRequest:list` keeps only the rows of allowed subjects for a scoped user and reads up to ten base pages to fill one answer (no 403; an answer can still hold fewer rows than `limit`, and it has no `total`); screens and nav stay at `access`. A scoped user must pass a `requestId` eq filter to `signatureSigner:list`, otherwise the query answers 403. `request` now also checks that the caller may read the document through the same decision as GET /files/:id; a file that is unknown or not readable answers `document_not_a_pdf`. `SIGNATURE_INVALID_LINK_REASON` is exported from `signature/static-sign`.
migration: Apps that request a signature on a file the caller cannot open through GET /files/:id bind it to a record the caller can read first. Apps with authorizeSubject pass a requestId eq filter to signatureSigner:list and do not rely on `total` of signatureRequest:list for scoped users.
